label: L=3 sequences, first copy step after the delimiter (t=4, output 2nd token)
explanation: Fires almost only in length-3 sequences, at step t=4: the first copy-phase step, where the fed-back first original token is the input and the second original token is output (93% of activation mass, 93% precision on dev). Its strongest activations are all here. Weaker leftover activity: the next step (t=5, L=3, ~4% of mass), and very weak firing on input h at t=1 in longer sequences (~2% of mass). Never fires at the delimiter step, at t=0, or at any step t>=6, and almost never in sequences with L>=4. A small number of L=3, t=4 steps stay silent (false positives often have a digit first token). Adding the t=1 h clause raised dev F1 only from 0.81 to 0.84, so the simple predicate was kept.

issues: Main claims check out. On test, (L==3)&(t==4) gets precision 0.942, recall 0.732, F1 0.824, mass recall 0.937. On dev, t=4 holds 93.4% of the mass and t=5 with L=3 holds 4.2%. The unit is silent at t=0, t=3, the delimiter step and every step with t>=6.

The 'h' at t=1 activity is a systematic, sharp class, not weak noise. (t==1)&(in_tok==h)&(first_tok in {a,p,s,f,r}) has precision 1.0 on dev (560/560). It covers about 17% of active steps by count, though only about 2% of the mass. The other agent said an 'h' clause only lifted dev F1 to 0.84, but that clause must have been wrong or too broad. A plain (t==1)&(in_tok==h) clause actually drops test F1 to 0.65, because 'h' after other first tokens does not fire.
Adding the precise bigram clause lifts test F1 from 0.824 to 0.925 (precision 0.953, recall 0.900). So the simple predicate leaves a systematic gap that is easy to recover.

The claim that silent L=3, t=4 steps often start with a digit is false. Precision is 0.929 when the first token is a digit and 0.945 when it is not, so there is no real difference. The false positives that remain lean toward first tokens r, n and m (precision 0.79), not digits.
The remaining misses are mostly t=5 with L=3 (the second copy step), at low-to-medium activation. That part of the explanation is accurate.
skeptic.revised_label: Mainly the first copy step after the delimiter in length-3 sequences (L=3, t=4). Also fires sharply on input 'h' at t=1 when the first token is a, p, s, f or r (low magnitude). Weak spillover at L=3, t=5.

final_label: Mainly the first copy step after the delimiter in length-3 sequences (L=3, t=4). Also fires sharply on input 'h' at t=1 when the first token is a, p, s, f or r (low magnitude). Weak spillover at L=3, t=5.
